name: redis-cli
description: Redis command line interface

flags.description: Server hostname (default 127.0.0.1)
Server port (default 6379)
Password for authentication (visible in process list and history; prefer REDISCLI_AUTH)
ACL username (Redis 6+), used together with -a or REDISCLI_AUTH
Connect using a URI, e.g. redis://user:pass@host:6379/0
Database number
Connect using TLS
List keys using SCAN (combine with --pattern)
Transfer raw Redis protocol for mass insertion
Repeat a command N times with an interval of i seconds
Prompt for the password with masked input
Cluster mode: follow MOVED/ASK redirections
Use the RESP3 protocol
Download an RDB snapshot from the server to a local file

examples.description: Authenticate without exposing the password in the process list
Connect with a URI over TLS (rediss://)
List matching keys without blocking the server
Connect to a Redis Cluster node and follow redirects
Take a remote RDB backup to a local file

notes: Default port is 6379
Use QUIT or exit to disconnect
Passing -a on the command line prints a warning because the password is visible to other users; use REDISCLI_AUTH instead

name: PING
description: Test Redis server connection
notes: Returns PONG on success

name: SET
description: Set string value for a key

flags.description: Set expiry in seconds
Set expiry in milliseconds
Only set if key doesn't exist
Only set if key exists
Expire at a Unix timestamp in seconds / milliseconds (Redis 6.2+)
Keep the existing TTL when overwriting (Redis 6.0+)
Return the old value stored at key (Redis 6.2+)

notes: Overwrites existing value and clears any TTL by default (use KEEPTTL to keep it)
SET ... NX EX is the preferred way to acquire a simple lock instead of SETNX + EXPIRE

name: GET
description: Get value of a key
notes: Returns nil if key doesn't exist

name: SETNX
description: Set a key only if it does not already exist

examples.description: Set only if missing; returns 1 if set, 0 if the key existed
Preferred modern equivalent with an expiry in a single atomic command

notes: Deprecated since Redis 2.6.12 in favour of SET key value NX
SETNX cannot set a TTL atomically; a crash between SETNX and EXPIRE leaves a lock forever

name: MSET
description: Set multiple keys to multiple values
notes: Atomic operation - all keys set at once

name: MGET
description: Get values of multiple keys
notes: Returns nil for non-existent keys

name: INCR
description: Increment integer value of a key
notes: Creates key with value 0 if doesn't exist
Atomic operation

name: DECR
description: Decrement integer value of a key
notes: Atomic operation

name: DEL
description: Delete one or more keys
notes: Returns number of keys deleted
Deleting a very large key blocks the server; use UNLINK to reclaim memory in the background

name: UNLINK
description: Delete keys and reclaim their memory asynchronously

examples.description: Remove a large key without blocking the server

notes: Removes the key immediately from the keyspace; memory is freed in a background thread
Prefer over DEL for large keys (Redis 4.0+)
Set lazyfree-lazy-user-del yes to make DEL behave like UNLINK

name: EXISTS
description: Check if key exists
notes: Returns count of existing keys

name: TYPE
description: Get the data type stored at a key

examples.description: Returns string, list, set, zset, hash, stream, or none

notes: Returns 'none' when the key does not exist

name: EXPIRE
description: Set key expiration time
notes: Use TTL to check remaining time

name: TTL
description: Get time to live for a key
notes: -1 means no expiry, -2 means key doesn't exist

name: PERSIST
description: Remove expiration from key
notes: Key will no longer expire

name: SCAN
description: Incrementally iterate keys

examples.description: Scan keys matching a pattern, examining ~1000 keys per call
Only return keys of a given type (Redis 6.0+)
Delete keys matching a pattern in batches from the shell

notes: Production-safe alternative to KEYS
Keep calling with the returned cursor until it returns 0
MATCH is applied after keys are fetched, so a call can return few or zero keys while the cursor is not finished
A key may be returned more than once; de-duplicate in your application if needed
Use HSCAN, SSCAN and ZSCAN to iterate large hashes, sets and sorted sets

name: KEYS
description: Find keys matching pattern
notes: AVOID in production - blocks server
Use SCAN for production workloads

name: HSET
description: Set hash field value
notes: Creates hash if doesn't exist
Accepts multiple field/value pairs since Redis 4.0; HMSET is deprecated

name: HGET
description: Get hash field value
notes: Returns nil if field doesn't exist

name: HGETALL
description: Get all fields and values in hash
notes: Returns empty list if key doesn't exist

name: HKEYS
description: Get all field names in a hash

examples.description: List field names of a hash

notes: O(N): for very large hashes use HSCAN instead

name: HDEL
description: Delete hash fields
notes: Returns number of fields deleted

name: HINCRBY
description: Increment the integer value of a hash field
notes: Creates the hash and field (starting from 0) if they don't exist
Atomic operation

name: HEXPIRE
description: Set a TTL on individual hash fields (Redis 7.4+)

examples.description: Only set the TTL if the field has none (also XX, GT, LT)
Remaining TTL per field in seconds (HPTTL for milliseconds)

notes: Returns one code per field: 1 set, 0 condition not met, 2 field deleted (TTL 0 or time in the past), -2 no such field
HTTL returns -1 for fields without a TTL and -2 for missing fields
HSET or HDEL of a field clears its TTL; HPEXPIRE, HEXPIREAT and HPEXPIREAT take milliseconds or absolute times

name: HSETEX
description: Set hash fields and their expiration in one atomic command (Redis 8.0+)

flags.description: TTL in seconds / milliseconds
Expire at a Unix time in seconds / milliseconds
Keep the fields' existing TTL
Only set if none of the fields exist
Only set if all of the fields already exist
Number of field/value pairs that follow

examples.description: Store a one-time code that expires in 5 minutes

examples.command: HSETEX cart:42 EX 3600 FIELDS 2 item:1 "2" item:7 "1"
examples.description: Set several fields with a 1 hour TTL

examples.command: HSETEX user:1 FNX EX 60 FIELDS 1 lock "worker-1"
examples.description: Per-field lock: only set if the field doesn't exist

notes: Returns 1 if all fields were set, 0 if none were (FNX/FXX condition failed)
Only one of EX, PX, EXAT, PXAT or KEEPTTL can be given

name: HGETEX / HGETDEL
description: Get hash fields while setting or removing their TTL, or get and delete them (Redis 8.0+)

examples.description: Read a field and slide its expiry to 30 minutes

examples.command: HGETEX user:1 PERSIST FIELDS 2 otp otp_attempts
examples.description: Read fields and remove their TTL
Read a one-time value and delete it atomically

notes: Missing fields come back as nil
HGETDEL deletes the key when its last field is removed

name: LPUSH
description: Prepend values to list
notes: Creates list if doesn't exist
RPUSH adds to end instead

name: RPUSH
description: Append values to list
notes: Creates list if doesn't exist

name: LPOP
description: Remove and get first list element
notes: Returns nil if list is empty
The count argument requires Redis 6.2+

name: RPOP
description: Remove and get last list element
notes: Returns nil if list is empty

name: BLPOP
description: Pop the first element of a list, blocking until one is available

examples.description: Pop from the first non-empty list, waiting up to 5 seconds

notes: Timeout is in seconds (decimals allowed since Redis 6.0); 0 blocks indefinitely
Returns the list name and the element, or nil on timeout
For reliable queues use BLMOVE to move items to a processing list

name: BRPOP
description: Pop the last element of a list, blocking until one is available

examples.description: Wait forever for an element at the tail

notes: LPUSH + BRPOP gives FIFO queue semantics
Returns nil when the timeout expires

name: LRANGE
description: Get range of list elements
notes: -1 means last element

name: LLEN
description: Get list length
notes: Returns 0 if key doesn't exist

name: SADD
description: Add members to set
notes: Ignores duplicate members

name: SREM
description: Remove members from a set
notes: Returns the number of members actually removed
The key is deleted when the set becomes empty

name: SMEMBERS
description: Get all members in set
notes: Order is not guaranteed

name: SISMEMBER
description: Check if value is member of set
notes: Returns 1 if member, 0 if not

name: SINTER
description: Intersect multiple sets
notes: Returns members present in all sets

name: SUNION
description: Union multiple sets
notes: Returns all members from all sets

name: SDIFF
description: Get members of the first set that are not in the other sets

examples.description: Find users who are not active
Store the difference in a new key

notes: Order of keys matters: the result is the first set minus all others

name: ZADD
description: Add members to sorted set with scores

examples.description: Update score only if the new score is greater (Redis 6.2+)

notes: Score determines sort order
Options: NX (only add), XX (only update), GT/LT (only update if greater/less), CH (return number changed)

name: ZRANGE
description: Get range of sorted set members

examples.description: Get all members (lowest to highest score)
Get top 10 (highest scores first) with scores
Get members with scores between 100 and 200
First 10 members with score greater than 100

notes: REV, BYSCORE, BYLEX and LIMIT require Redis 6.2+ (they replace ZREVRANGE and ZRANGEBYSCORE)
( makes a score bound exclusive; -inf and +inf are open bounds

name: ZSCORE
description: Get the score of a member in a sorted set
notes: Returns nil if the member or key does not exist

name: ZRANK
description: Get rank of member in sorted set
notes: Rank is 0-based

name: MULTI / EXEC
description: Run a group of commands atomically as a transaction

examples.command:
MULTI
INCR stock:42
LPUSH orders:recent 42
EXEC
examples.description: Queue commands and execute them atomically
Abort a transaction started with MULTI

notes: Commands between MULTI and EXEC are queued and run without interleaving from other clients
There is no rollback: if one command fails at runtime, the others still run
Use WATCH for optimistic locking, or a Lua script / FUNCTION for logic that depends on read values

name: WATCH
description: Watch keys so a following transaction aborts if they change

examples.command:
WATCH balance:alice
GET balance:alice
MULTI
DECRBY balance:alice 50
EXEC
examples.description: Check-and-set: EXEC returns nil if balance:alice changed after WATCH

notes: If EXEC returns nil (null array) the transaction did not run; retry the whole read-modify-write
WATCH is cleared after EXEC or DISCARD

name: PUBLISH
description: Publish message to channel
notes: Returns number of subscribers that received message
Messages are fire-and-forget: subscribers that are offline miss them; use Streams for durable messaging

name: SUBSCRIBE
description: Subscribe to channels
notes: Blocks waiting for messages
Use UNSUBSCRIBE to stop

name: XADD
description: Append an entry to a stream

flags.description: Let Redis generate the entry ID
Approximately cap the stream length
Do not create the stream if it doesn't exist

examples.description: Add an entry with an auto-generated ID
Add while trimming to roughly 10,000 entries

notes: IDs are <milliseconds>-<sequence>
Without trimming (MAXLEN/MINID or XTRIM) streams grow forever

name: XREAD / XREADGROUP
description: Read entries from one or more streams, optionally via a consumer group

examples.description: Read the first 10 entries from the start
Wait up to 5 seconds for new entries only

examples.command: XREADGROUP GROUP workers worker-1 COUNT 10 BLOCK 2000 STREAMS events >
examples.description: Read new messages for this consumer

notes: $ means only entries added after the call; > (with groups) means never-delivered messages
Unacknowledged messages stay in the pending list; inspect with XPENDING and reclaim with XAUTOCLAIM

name: JSON.SET / JSON.GET
description: Store, read and update JSON documents (built into Redis 8+)

examples.description: Create a JSON document at the root path
Add or replace a field (string values need JSON quotes)

notes: New documents must be created at the root ($); NX/XX make JSON.SET conditional
Before Redis 8 this required the RedisJSON module or Redis Stack
$ paths return arrays of matches; JSON.GET key with no path returns the whole document

name: FT.CREATE
description: Create a secondary index over hashes or JSON documents for search and vector queries (Redis 8+)

examples.command: FT.CREATE idx:posts ON HASH PREFIX 1 post: SCHEMA title TEXT SORTABLE published_at NUMERIC SORTABLE category TAG
examples.description: Index hashes whose keys start with post:

examples.command: FT.CREATE idx:users ON JSON PREFIX 1 user: SCHEMA $.name AS name TEXT $.tags[*] AS tags TAG $.logins AS logins NUMERIC
examples.description: Index JSON documents using JSONPath aliases

examples.command: FT.CREATE idx:docs ON HASH PREFIX 1 doc: SCHEMA embedding VECTOR HNSW 6 TYPE FLOAT32 DIM 768 DISTANCE_METRIC COSINE

examples.description: Show index definition and indexing progress
Drop the index but keep the documents

notes: Existing keys matching the prefix are indexed in the background; new writes are indexed automatically
Before Redis 8 this required the RediSearch module or Redis Stack
WARNING: FT.DROPINDEX ... DD also deletes the indexed documents

name: FT.SEARCH
description: Query a search index with full-text, numeric, tag and vector (KNN) filters

examples.command: FT.SEARCH idx:posts "@title:redis @category:{news}" SORTBY published_at DESC LIMIT 0 10
examples.description: Field and tag filter, newest first
Numeric range, returning only the title
Count matching documents without returning them

examples.command: FT.SEARCH idx:docs "*=>[KNN 5 @embedding $vec AS score]" PARAMS 2 vec <float32-blob> SORTBY score DIALECT 2
examples.description: Top 5 nearest vectors (pass the blob from client code)

notes: LIMIT defaults to 0 10; the first element of the reply is the total match count
PARAMS requires DIALECT 2 or higher
Use FT.AGGREGATE for grouping, counting and reshaping results

name: VADD
description: Add an element and its embedding to a vector set (Redis 8.0+)

flags.description: Vector given as n float values (or FP32 for a little-endian binary blob)
Attach JSON attributes for filtered search
Quantization: int8 (default), binary, or full precision
Reduce dimensionality with random projection
HNSW graph links per node (default 16) and build effort (default 200)

examples.description: Add an element with a 3-dimensional vector

notes: Vector sets are a sorted-set-like type for similarity search; no index definition is needed (unlike FT.CREATE)
Every element in a set must have the same dimension (after REDUCE)

name: VSIM
description: Find the most similar elements in a vector set, optionally filtered by attributes (Redis 8.0+)

flags.description: Query by an existing element, or by a vector
Number of results
Return similarity scores (1 = identical, 0 = opposite)
Return each element's JSON attributes
Filter on attributes, e.g. '.price < 100 and .category == "shoes"'
Search effort; higher improves recall at the cost of speed

examples.command: VSIM products ELE sku:123 COUNT 5 WITHSCORES
examples.description: 5 elements most similar to sku:123, with scores
Nearest neighbours of a query vector

examples.command: VSIM products ELE sku:123 COUNT 10 FILTER '.category == "shoes" and .price < 100'
VSIM products ELE sku:123 COUNT 10 FILTER '.brand in ["acme", "globex"]' FILTER-EF 1000
examples.description: Rare filter: let the engine inspect more candidates

notes: Filter expressions use dot notation for top-level attribute fields; elements missing the attribute don't match
TRUTH forces an exact linear scan, useful for measuring recall

name: INFO
description: Get Redis server information
notes: Sections: server, clients, memory, persistence, stats, replication, cpu, cluster, keyspace

name: DBSIZE
description: Get number of keys in current database
notes: Fast O(1) operation

name: CONFIG GET
description: Read server configuration parameters

examples.description: Get all parameters matching a pattern

notes: Managed services (ElastiCache, Memorystore, etc.) often disable or restrict CONFIG

name: CONFIG SET
description: Change server configuration at runtime

examples.description: Evict least recently used keys when full

notes: Changes are lost on restart unless you run CONFIG REWRITE or edit redis.conf
Be careful on production servers: some settings (e.g. maxmemory) take effect immediately

name: ACL SETUSER
description: Create or modify a Redis user with its password, key patterns and allowed commands

examples.description: App user limited to app:* keys and channels, no dangerous commands
Show all users and their rules
Delete a user and disconnect its sessions
Write users to the aclfile configured in redis.conf

notes: Rules are applied on top of existing ones; start with reset to define a user from scratch
Redis 8 adds JSON, search, time series and probabilistic commands to @read/@write, so existing +@read/+@write rules grant more than before; review ACLs when upgrading
Use placeholders here: real passwords in commands end up in shell history

name: CLIENT LIST
description: List connected clients and their state

examples.description: Show all connections with address, age, idle time and last command
Name the current connection so it is easy to identify

notes: Useful for spotting connection leaks: check 'age' and 'idle' columns
INFO clients gives aggregate counts

name: SLOWLOG GET
description: Show recent commands that exceeded the slow-log threshold

examples.description: Show the 10 most recent slow commands
Count entries in the slow log

notes: Threshold is slowlog-log-slower-than in microseconds (default 10000 = 10 ms)
Execution time excludes network I/O, so slow clients won't show up here

name: MEMORY USAGE
description: Estimate how many bytes a key and its value use

examples.description: Show memory used by a key in bytes
Measure all elements of a nested type exactly (slower)

notes: For aggregates it samples 5 elements by default; SAMPLES 0 checks all of them

name: OBJECT
description: Inspect the internal encoding and access stats of a key

examples.description: Show internal encoding, e.g. listpack, hashtable, int, embstr
Seconds since the key was last accessed (LRU policies)
Access frequency counter (only with an LFU maxmemory-policy)

name: redis-cli --bigkeys
description: Scan the keyspace to find the largest key of each type

flags.description: Report the biggest key per type by element count
Report the biggest keys by memory usage
Combine --bigkeys and --memkeys with size distribution and a top-N list
Number of top keys to show with --keystats (default 10)
Find frequently accessed keys (requires an LFU maxmemory-policy)
Sleep between SCAN batches to reduce load

examples.description: Find the largest key of each type
Find keys using the most memory
Throttle the scan on a busy server
Top 20 keys by size plus per-type distribution
Find the most frequently accessed keys

notes: Uses SCAN, so it is safe to run on production but adds load; run against a replica if possible

name: redis-cli --latency
description: Measure round-trip latency to the Redis server

flags.description: Continuously sample latency (min/max/avg in ms)
Print a new sample line every 15 seconds (change with -i)
Show a latency distribution spectrum
Measure the host's own latency (run on the Redis server)
Rolling stats: keys, memory, clients, requests

examples.description: Measure latency to a remote server
Check host/VM baseline latency for 30 seconds

notes: Press Ctrl+C to stop
Use LATENCY DOCTOR inside redis-cli for server-side latency analysis (requires latency-monitor-threshold)

name: FLUSHDB
description: Delete all keys in current database
notes: WARNING: irreversible - deletes every key in the selected database
Often blocked in production with ACLs (-flushdb or -@dangerous) or rename-command

name: FLUSHALL
description: Delete all keys in all databases

examples.description: Clear all databases in the background

notes: WARNING: irreversible - clears ALL data in ALL databases
Restrict it with ACLs (e.g. -@dangerous) in production

name: SAVE
description: Synchronously save dataset to disk
notes: SAVE blocks all clients until the snapshot is written
Use BGSAVE in production

name: BGSAVE
description: Asynchronously save dataset to disk
notes: Non-blocking operation: forks a child process to write the RDB snapshot
Forking a large dataset can briefly use extra memory
Check completion with LASTSAVE or INFO persistence

name: LASTSAVE
description: Get the Unix time of the last successful RDB save

examples.description: Get the timestamp of the last successful save
See rdb_last_bgsave_status and AOF status in more detail

notes: Poll LASTSAVE after BGSAVE to see when the snapshot has finished
